name: New Mexico
sources: Brackets: NMSA 7-2-7 as amended by 2024 HB 252 for tax years 2025+ — https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/24%20Regular/final/HB0252.pdf; 2025 tax rate table — https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/NM/2025/2025trt.pdf; rates unchanged for 2026 per 2026 withholding formula — https://news.bloombergtax.com/payroll/new-mexico-releases-2026-withholding-formula

Capital gains deduction: NMSA 7-2-34 as amended by 2024 HB 252 (lesser of net capital gain or $2,500; half for married filing separately; 40% of up to $1M only for sale of a New Mexico business) — https://www.nmlegis.gov/Sessions/24%20Regular/final/HB0252.pdf
Standard or itemized deduction as claimed on the federal return: 2025 PIT-1 instructions — https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/NM/2025/2025pit-ez-ins.pdf

Deduction for certain dependents ($4,000 for all but one dependent, MFJ/HoH only) and low/middle-income exemption: NM TRD — https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2020.01.24_NM-Income-Tax-changes-for-the-coming-filing-season.pdf; 2025 PIT-1 instructions
provisional: The 2026 PIT-1 is not yet published; brackets and the $2,500 capital gains deduction are statutory for 2025 onward with no 2026 change found. 2026 HB 93 (standard deduction at 205% of federal) was introduced; its enactment was not confirmed and it is not reflected
Itemized property tax capped at the federal SALT cap ($40,400; $20,200 MFS); the federal cap's phase-down above $505,000 MAGI is not applied
notes: New Mexico's $4,000 deduction for each dependent after the first (joint and head-of-household returns) and its low- and middle-income exemptions are not included.
The capital gains deduction is limited to $2,500; the larger 40% deduction for selling a New Mexico business is not included.
